shorts.title: Is the Bermuda Triangle Real? 🔍 Meatball Investigates
shorts.description:
Ships vanish in the Bermuda Triangle. Supposedly. Even the rescue plane sent after Flight 19 was lost, most likely in an explosion. The 'Bermuda Triangle' name comes from a 1964 magazine story by Vincent Gaddis.

#shorts #meatballinvestigates #weirdhistory #mystery #meatballmyths

shorts.title: Operation Northwoods: The Conspiracy That Was TRUE 🔍
shorts.description:
US generals once planned fake attacks. Seriously. One idea in the plan: fake the shoot-down of a civilian airliner with a remote-controlled drone. The memo was declassified in 1997.

#shorts #meatballinvestigates #weirdhistory #mystery #meatballmyths

shorts.title: What REALLY Crashed at Roswell? 🔍 Meatball Investigates
shorts.description:
The Roswell cover-up was real. Not aliens. Project Mogul's balloons carried microphones to listen for Soviet nuclear tests. The Air Force's reports came out in 1994-1997.

#shorts #meatballinvestigates #weirdhistory #mystery #meatballmyths

Photos (Wikimedia Commons, NOAA, NARA, iNaturalist, Openverse), cropped and color-adjusted: Roswell debris, 1947: "Ramey-dubose-debris.jpg" by Fort Worth Star-Telegram (Public domain), via Wikimedia Commons, "Marcel-roswell-debris 0.jpg" by Fort Worth Star-Telegram (Public domain), via Wikimedia Commons; Weather balloon launch (NOAA): "wea01144" by NOAA Photo Library (CC BY 2.0), via flickr; Project Mogul balloon train: "Mogul balloon train USAF 1995.png" by United States Air Force (Public domain), via Wikimedia Commons; The Roswell Report: Case Closed: Case Closed: "The Roswell Report - Case Closed.jpg" by James McAndrew (USAF) (Public domain), via Wikimedia Commons. creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: What did you think crashed? 👽 aliens / 🎈 balloon

shorts.title: The Great Emu War: Australia Lost to Birds 🔍
shorts.description:
Australia went to war with emus. And lost. The soldiers fired almost 10,000 rounds. About 20,000 emus had moved onto the wheat farms.

#shorts #meatballinvestigates #weirdhistory #mystery #meatballmyths

shorts.title: The Dancing Plague of 1518 Was REAL 🔍
shorts.description:
In 1518, a town couldn't stop dancing. It happened in Strasbourg in July 1518. The physician Paracelsus wrote about it a few years later.

#shorts #meatballinvestigates #weirdhistory #mystery #meatballmyths

shorts.title: Lightning Never Strikes Twice? WRONG 🔍
shorts.description:
Lightning never strikes twice? Wrong. Park ranger Roy Sullivan holds the record: struck by lightning 7 times between 1942 and 1977, and survived all of them.

#shorts #meatballinvestigates #weirdhistory #mystery #meatballmyths
